name: HERA-B
notes: Hall: the West Hall of HERA (arXiv:1605.03459); Placed at the DESY Hamburg campus site (campus-grade): the East and West halls of the HERA ring have no coordinate in any fetched source (OpenStreetMap names only the North hall and a building "HERA West 50", whose position does not fit the ring geometry), so no hall point is asserted.
The stated purpose was the study of CP violation in the B-Bbar system; the sources fetched report cross-section measurements, not a CP-violation result, and the record does not claim one.

physics_goals.quote: The HERA-B experiment [19,20] in the West Hall was built to use collisions of the proton beam halo with a wire target in order to produce B-mesons for the study of CP violation in the B − B̄ system.
physics_goals.value: Produce B mesons with wire targets in the halo of the HERA proton beam to study CP violation in the B-Bbar system

summary.plain: HERA-B was an experiment at DESY that placed thin wires in the halo of HERA's 920 GeV proton beam so that protons struck the wires and produced B mesons and J/psi particles, built to study the matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) in B meson decays. It ran from 2000 to 2003.
summary.technical: HERA-B: fixed-target forward spectrometer in the HERA West hall using wire targets (carbon, titanium, tungsten) in the halo of the 920 GeV/c proton beam; vertex detector, tracking, RICH, calorimeter and muon systems with a dilepton trigger; commissioning run 2000, main data in the 2002-2003 HERA running period; measured the b-bbar and J/psi production cross sections but did not reach its CP-violation goal.
